extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors, broadcasters, journalists, and censorship officials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for journalists, newspapers and broadcasters on what wartime information may be published or broadcast, including revisions to the Office of Censorship code and recommended national censorship measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit war production contracts from censorship restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Omits from censorship restriction war production contracts because other Government agencies have suitable controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised code removes war production contracts from the Office of Censorship's restrictions, indicating those matters are handled by other government agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove category 'capable of adaption for war production' from restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Omits from the code the category 'capable of adaption for war production' from restrictions on secret war designs and formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material merely 'capable of adaption for war production' is no longer automatically restricted by the censorship code except where other provisions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow publication of exact types of war products except for secret designs/weapons/formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Omits, except in the case of secret designs, weapons and formulas, former restrictions on publishing exact types of war products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General reporting on types of war products is permitted under the revised code, but explicit details of secret designs, weapons and formulas remain prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit local and national roundup stories on war production with limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits local and national roundup stories on war production as long as they do not reveal production rates of specific products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roundup or summary stories about war production may be published/broadcast provided they avoid disclosing production rates or other specifics that could aid enemy intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on publishing 'secret plans' without appropriate authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Added to the code is a ban against publishing 'secret plans' without appropriate authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material characterized as a 'secret plan' must not be published unless proper authorization is obtained from the appropriate authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal questionable censorship requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspapers in a special note: 'whenever anyone else, in any part of the country, makes a request which appears unreasonable or not in harmony with the code, you are at liberty to appeal at once to the Office of Censorship.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors who receive requests they judge unreasonable under the code are explicitly encouraged to seek a prompt ruling from the Office of Censorship rather than acquiesce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended scope for continental communications censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: A committee asked American countries to enforce censorship of all communications to or from: (1) any of the Axis powers or occupied countries; (2) any non-American nation not at war with the Axis; (3) any American country which has not broken relations with all members of the Axis, or having broken relations has not yet banned communications with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation defines three classes of foreign/neutral correspondents and diplomatic channels for which strict censorship is urged to prevent espionage and transmission of intelligence to the Axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast/network conformity and limits on inflammatory commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Network editors have been reminded that broadcasts 'must conform to regulations' and that commentators who depart from prepared texts to discuss controversial subjects in an 'inflammatory manner' may violate policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasters should adhere to prepared scripts and network regulations; departure into inflammatory commentary (as alleged in relation to Walter Winchell and Drew Pearson) risks censorship or corrective action by networks and may be scrutinized by oversight bodies.
